To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the data quality of SFX data is not affected by the use of self- seeding, by crystal-to-crystal unit-cell parameter variations, or by the presence or absence of post-selection of crystals based on the diffraction quality.
self-seeded data do not provide any advantage over SASE data and that, at present, the main limitation in SFX data quality is due to variations in crystal size and quality, and not to the X-ray beam.

the use of self- seeded pulses at FELs is not expected to improve the data quality in Monte Carlo-integrated serial femtosecond X-ray crystallography, and that crystal post-selection does not affect the quality of the resulting data either.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of the Monte Carlo-integrated diffraction patterns obtained from SFX data.
the question: How many crystals are really needed for accurate data collection in SFX?
the question of whether SFX data quality could be improved, but the experiments performed here suggest that this is not the case.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quality of SFX data collected at FELs is not limited by any of the factors studied here, and that, as a result, the Monte Carlo-integrated intensities are accurate to within the statistical uncertainties.

, in the absence of any other significant sources of variation, the number of crystals required for Monte Carlo integration is determined only by the number of independent reflections in the data set, and is therefore independent of the mode of operation of the FEL.
the use of self- seeding has no influence on the quality of SFX data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the moment, the quality of SFX data is limited by the intrinsic quality of the crystals and not by other factors.
the Monte Carlo integration works very well in SFX and that the number of crystals needed to obtain a converged data set is much smaller than previously thought.
the data quality is dominated by variations between crystals and that the use of self seeding does not improve the quality of the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SFX data quality is not affected significantly by any of the sources of variation that were tested.

, in spite of the fact that the SASE pulses are very spiky, this does not appear to be a significant source of variation in SFX data, and the Monte Carlo integration scheme is able to converge to accurate data with only a few thousand diffraction snapshots, even in SASE mode.

, at least in the cases investigated, the data quality of SFX experiments is not compromised by the SASE mode of operation of the FEL, and the use of selfseeding does not improve the accuracy of the data.
